checks: Checked 207a0b33a5d3a235 §§2–4 and the supporting representation in §1 against the frozen statement and proof. Its scope includes arbitrary Borel probability and explicitly assumes the depth region is nonempty.

For a large-mass closed halfspace, a parallel closed halfspace through an excluded point has mass below alpha. Conversely, continuity from below inside the open complement of a bad closed halfspace provides a large-mass closed halfspace excluding the point. This handles boundary atoms with the indicated strict inequalities.

The finite exclusion uses compact S. The expanded grid hull contains C in its interior and converges to it. At a depth-region point every expanded inequality has slack, even when the depth region itself is lower dimensional. A sequence of residual mixed-lattice points would limit to S while satisfying all original K_i, a contradiction.

The sign in Farkas elimination is correct. A positive kernel vector on a minimal support has a one-dimensional restricted kernel by independent perturbation to the orthant boundary, so the rank bound gives d+1. Subtracting maximal multiples preserves the kernel and drops support. When d=0 the rays are singleton supports.

A nontrivial projected inequality tight at a relative interior point of a facet has the same supporting hyperplane and positive orientation. Its positive sum of constituent slacks is zero at every lift in Q, establishing the claimed simultaneous contact.

The projected closed facet halfspaces miss the integer lattice. The selected strict exteriors cover all S, and their measures are bounded by finite sums of the constituent strict exterior masses. Positivity of the number of constituents yields the strict mass bound.

dependencies.mapping: Use the finite mixed-lattice Helly theorem documented in the proof with continuous dimension zero and integer dimension n. For more than 2^n actual closed facet halfspaces use its contrapositive on their lattice-empty intersection. For at most 2^n use the whole family.

overlap.comparison: Gives the same lattice Helly input and the associated numerical depth bound for arbitrary Borel measures. Its conclusion supplies neither the auxiliary outer polytope nor facet lifts and their contacts.

Gives sparse exact mass-level circuits at regular contacts of the actual projected depth region, with extra full-volume and normal-cone hypotheses. Here the contacts are on the projection of an auxiliary full-dimensional outer polytope and the original exterior masses are strictly below alpha.

Constructs a nonvertical closed-cap cover at the exact depth budget for a full-dimensional fiber-volume setting. Its conclusion does not give projected facet certificates, and its cap class, budget and measure hypotheses differ.

readability: The lift contact refers to Q, and the facet exterior is read in the ambient space via base projection. The strict mass estimate concerns the lifted exterior and uses support on S.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The construction gives a full-dimensional lattice-excluded outer polytope, sparse certificates with contacts on all its facet lifts, and the claimed strict exterior cover and mass bounds.
